Consonant

/KON-suh-nuhnt/ - the stress falls on KON · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Consonant means in agreement or keeping with something.

The counselor's advice was consonant with everything the coach had preached all season: rest is training too.

Worked Example

When the shelter wrote its first paid-staff policy, the director read it against the founding letters twice — every clause, she said, had to be consonant with what the volunteers had built.

Consonant with is for deep keeping — values, spirit, principles — not the mere absence of clash. Two apps that avoid crashing are compatible; a decision that positively rings true to a tradition is consonant with it. The word promises harmony, not just tolerance.

How Consonant Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

compatible

compatible: able to exist or work together without clashing — the minimum, where consonant is a positive fit

harmonious

harmonious: pleasingly combined — closest to consonant, but more about beauty than principle

Antonyms

jarring

jarring: clashing so hard it startles

contrary

contrary: pointed the opposite way entirely

How Strong Is It? — compatible → consonant → indistinguishable

compatible vs. consonant

compatible vs. consonant: Compatible is the floor — two things can share a room without fighting, and that is all it claims.

indistinguishable vs. consonant

indistinguishable vs. consonant: Indistinguishable goes further than consonant — a consonant addition still reads as new work in an old spirit; an indistinguishable one cannot be told from the original at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — con-

Prefix — con-: together

Root — son-

Root — son-: sound

Suffix — -ant

Suffix — -ant: -ing; in the manner of

Put it together

Put it together: Con- (together) + son- (sound) + -ant = sounding together. Latin consonare described notes that ring well at the same time. English kept the ear's judgment and widened it: a plan consonant with a tradition 'sounds right' beside it — no clash, no false note.

Use the root in a new word: sonic

Use the root in a new word: sonic: The jet crossed the sonic barrier with a boom that rattled every window on the base.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / evaluative

Consonant is an evaluator's word — reviews, rulings, mission statements — and it always takes with: consonant with the charter, with the style, with the founder's intent. Compatible sets a lower bar (no clash); harmonious praises the blend itself. Say consonant when something new keeps faith with something old.
